title: Cross-metric correlated anomaly detection + RCA enrichment for console usage alerts
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: We currently surface per-metric anomalies (cost spikes, latency increases, token usage jumps) independently which generates noisy alerts and often misses correlated incidents that span multiple metrics. That causes paging fatigue and slow triage for customers and SREs.

Goal: Build a backend service and pipeline stage that detects correlated anomalies across usage/cost/latency signals, groups related events into a single incident, and enriches alerts with likely root-cause signals (model_id, region, customer_tier, route, release tag) to enable faster triage. The implementation should be production-safe, have controlled false-positive rates, and be compatible with both hosted and Dedicated telemetry streams.

Scope:
- New anomaly detection microservice (anomaly-aggregator) that consumes normalized time-series from the usage analytics pipeline.
- Cross-metric correlation logic using graph clustering + Bayesian change-point scoring to identify multi-signal incidents.
- RCA enrichment step that joins anomalies to request-level attributes in the analytics warehouse and billing tables.
- Alert grouping rules and priority scoring to reduce noise.
- Integration with existing console alerting and pager channels (Slack, Opsgenie).

Out of scope for this ticket: UI redesign for console alert list, per-customer SLA automation, on-prem standalone agent changes.
acceptance_criteria: Anomaly-aggregator service deployed to staging and consumes normalized time-series (cost, latency_p95, request_count) from the analytics topic.
Detector groups anomalies across at least two signal types and emits a single grouped incident record with confidence score and top-3 enriched attributes.
False-positive rate on historical test set is <= 8% and precision/recall measured and documented.
Console alerting pipeline receives grouped incident webhooks and displays incident metadata in staging dashboard.
Runbook snippet for on-call created describing how to interpret correlated incidents and how to silence groupings per-customer.
implementation_notes: Input signals: normalized, per-tenant timeseries at 1m granularity for cost, latency_p50/p95, token_count, successful_requests, error_rate.

Detection algorithm: hybrid approach — use Bayesian online change-point detection per signal to get event boundaries, then build a temporal graph where nodes are events and edges connect events that overlap in time and share strong feature similarity. Cluster graph to form incident groups.

Enrichment: when an incident group is formed, run a fast join against the recent window of request logs and billing table to surface top attributes (model_id, region, route, plan_tier, commit/rollout tag). Precompute inverted indexes for model_id and route to avoid full scans.
Scoring: compute priority = weighted sum of (customers_impacted_count, cost_delta_pct, latency_p95_delta, duration_hours, confidence). Tunable weights stored in config service.
Backpressure: aggregator must tolerate bursty input; use Kafka consumer partitioning by tenant and in-memory sliding window per tenant with eviction policy.

Fail-safes: if enrichment store is unavailable, emit grouped incident with 'enrichment_delayed' flag and retry asynchronously. Ensure no high-severity paging for low-confidence groups unless human override.
Privacy: do not include PII in alerts. Strip request identifiers and only surface hashed customer ids and aggregated counts.
Compatibility: support both 'hosted' telemetry schema and 'dedicated' telemetry envelope; map fields during ingestion stage.
Observability: instrument per-tenant processing latency, enrichment latency, grouping rate, and false_positive_counter; expose Prometheus metrics and traces.
Rollout: create canary config to enable grouping for 10% of tenants, measure alert noise delta before broader rollout.
data_schema_changes: Add 'enrichment_window_start' and 'enrichment_window_end' fields to incident record schema.
Add 'group_confidence' and 'top_enriched_attributes' array to grouped incident payload.
Normalized timeseries topic must include 'tenant_hash' field and 'route' dimension for cross-correlation.
Billing table snapshot that is fast to query for last 2 hours should be exported to analytics namespace (daily jobs already exist; add 1m snapshot job).
pipeline_changes: New consumer in analytics pipeline: anomaly-aggregator subscribes to 'normalized-metrics-v1' Kafka topic.
Add a lightweight preprocessor to map dedicated telemetry envelope into the canonical normalized schema.
New enrichment micro-batch job that writes recent request attribute aggregates into an in-memory cache (Redis) for fast joins.
Hook into existing alert webhook sink; grouped incident -> alert builder -> Slack/opsgenie. Update schema contract for grouped incidents.
Add e2e integration test in pipeline CI that replays historical traffic with known correlated incidents and validates output groupings.

comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Kaur: Created ticket after spike with SRE and Observability PM. Spike validated feasibility of Bayesian change-point + graph clustering approach on 7 days of telemetry. Next: design doc and infra spike for Redis enrichment cache.

2026-03-11 - Diego Morales: Implemented prototype consumer that reads normalized metrics and emits event boundaries for single signals. Found that p95 latency noise in low-traffic tenants results in spurious change points; plan to add tenant-specific smoothing and minimum-activity thresholds.

2026-03-12 - Priya Shah (Observability PM): Requested that priority scoring include 'customer_tier' and 'sla_class' so enterprise customers surface higher. Also suggested an 'auto-mute' window per-customer to avoid re-alerting on recurring maintenance events.
2026-03-12 - Security review note by Julio Ramos: Confirmed no PII in enrichment; asked to ensure hashed tenant IDs use project-wide salt. Action: add salt rotation note to implementation.

2026-03-13 - Diego Morales: Decided on precomputing attribute aggregates into Redis with a TTL of 10m to keep joins O(1). Trade-off: small window lowers completeness of RCA for very low-volume events; acceptable for initial rollout.
2026-03-13 - Aisha Kaur: Scheduling canary rollout during low-traffic weekend window (2026-04-03 to 2026-04-05). Need SRE on-call and runbook completion before enabling canary.
2026-03-13 - Action items added: create e2e test dataset (Diego), implement tenant smoothing (ENG-20124), add canary flag in feature flags service (ENG-19011).
2026-03-13 - QA note: We'll validate precision/recall using labeled historical incidents from last 90 days and document results in the design Confluence page.
